invariants: Session events require the exact owned Session object, not merely a matching id; claimed inbox events/errors require the exact owned Agent.
Only the in-flight ACP message's claimed turn may supply its durable ending; neighbor, old-turn, same-id impostor and unclaimed-message events cannot overwrite it.
Explicit cancellation wins over a later completed event and prompt settlement waits for Agent quiescence.
Enqueue, idle, durable-turn and interval failures release only their exact prompt admission slot; same-turn errors use the durable ending.
Canonical run_profile/Loader/real AgentLoop integration claims a real turn and releases the Agent without replacing providers with a legacy harness.
open_questions: Full ACP stdio registration, output drain, request-signal cancellation, persistent list/resume/close/config and MCP/permissions remain a separate provider/consumer contract.
Review rc.1 provider/consumer changes and obtain new acceptance; alpha observations cannot certify this revision.
identity: Exact owned Agent, exact owned Session, accepted message id and claimed turn identify one prompt; no global turn-end broadcast settlement.
ownership: The ACP SessionRecord owns its one prompt slot; all error paths clear only the local identity they admitted. Context owns reversible handlers and Agent disposal.
ordering: Admit content, assign the slot before followup, correlate inbox claim, read only the same turn ending, wait for idle, settle or fail, then clear the same slot in finally.
errors: Cancellation cannot be overwritten by late normal completion; actual turn/interval failures reject instead of falsely reporting end_turn, and rejected admission/idle leaves no occupied slot.
cancellation: The client cancel operation marks only its owned prompt, cancels only its Agent and preserves the quiescence boundary. Complete SDK request cancellation is not claimed.
adaptation: Python 3.8.10 native bridge handler contract only. Original 139-test ACP source baseline is distinct from bounded Python coverage; no full ACP wire/MCP parity or Win7 certification is claimed.

rc1_review.scope: The revised executable corpus and current Source inputs define bounded acceptance; historical alpha reviews remain historical.
